ITQAN:v4p431/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.claim: The only adjacent kāf-kāf sequences without an intervening letter occur in “manāsikakum” and “mā salakakum.”
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.anchor: ولا كافان كذلك إلا ﴿ مناسككم ﴾ ﴿ ما سلككم ﴾

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.claim: Nature’s manifestations argue for the Hereafter and expose heedlessness; the Qur’an warns so people can prepare, while evaders are left with stubbornness as their excuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.anchor: An argument on the Hereafter from the manifestations of nature is presented

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r5.claim: Each soul is held for its own deeds, and only its deeds can free it or lead it to Hell; neither another’s deeds nor intercession benefits someone else.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r5.anchor: each person will be held in pledge for his own deeds

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r6.claim: The people of the right hand are the victors in Paradise and ask those in Hell what brought them there; the latter openly confess their crimes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r6.anchor: the crimes which led them to their state of doom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p56/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p56/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p56/r2.claim: The question about what brought the sinners into Hell is asked by the companions of Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p56/r2.anchor: This question shall be posed to the companions of Hell by the companions of Paradise

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p338/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p338/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p338/r4.claim: The criminals first lacked the Muslim practices of prayer and almsgiving, then moved to the greater sin of disbelief and denial of Judgment, echoing 90:11 and 90:17.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p338/r4.anchor: لم يكونوا متصفين بخصائل الإسلام من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة، ثم ارتقوا

NAHHAS:v5p72/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p72/r9.claim: The question 'what brought you to Saqar?' is spoken by people who did not sin.
NAHHAS:v5p72/r9.anchor: فهذا كلام من لم يعمل خطيئة

NAHHAS:v5p72/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r10.speaker: ابن الزبير
NAHHAS:v5p72/r10.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna reports ʿAmr ibn Dīnār hearing Ibn al-Zubayr's interpretive reading; the transmission is sound.
NAHHAS:v5p72/r10.anchor: قال سمعت ابن الزبير يقرأ ( يتساءلون عن المجرمين يا فلان ما سلكك في سقر ) وهذه القراءة على التفسير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398/r11.claim: سلك means admitted; Abu Wajza al-Saʿdi's poem uses the verb of limbs entering a hide.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p398/r11.anchor: وسلك معناه: أدخل، ومنه قول أبي وجزة السعدي:

ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r7.claim: The question asks the criminals directly, or through an intermediary, what offense caused them to enter seqar.
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r7.anchor: Bu sual, ashâb-ı yemînin birbirlerine değil de mücrimlere bizzat veya bi’l-vâsıta sordukları sualdir.

ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r8.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r8.claim: Keššāf argues the question is not the righteous asking one another: that construction would say “what put them in seqar”; the wording reports the question actually posed to the criminals.
ELMALILI:74:32-56#2/r8.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf der ki: Bu, ashâb-ı yemînin birbirlerine suallerini beyan değildir.

BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r1.speaker: يروى
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r1.claim: A report says God shows Paradise's inhabitants the people of Hell while they are in Hell, and they ask what led them into Saqar.
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r1.anchor: (يروى) : إن الله يطلع أهل الجنة وهم في الجنة حتى يرون أهل النار وهم في النار

BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r2.claim: The question is asked to reproach and intensify the sinners' regret, and to make the account a warning for its hearers.
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r2.anchor: توبيخا لهم وتحسيرا ولتكون حكاية الله ذلك في كتابه تذكرة للسامعين

BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r3.claim: سلككم means inserted you into it, from inserting a thread into a needle; it derives from اسلك, not from سلوك meaning to walk.
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r3.anchor: من سلكت الخيط في الأبرة سلكا أي أدخلته فيها فهو من اسلك بمعنى الإدخال

BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r4.claim: The phrase ما سلككم is parsed with an implied saying as a circumstantial clause.
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r4.anchor: مقدر بقول هو حال مقدرة من فاعل يتساءلون أي قائلين

BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr assimilates the first ك into the next in سلككم; the other readers pronounce both distinctly.
BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمر وسلكم بإدغام الكاف في الكاف والباقون بالإظهار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p273/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p273/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p273/r1.claim: The criminals asked about are polytheists, and the question asks what put them into Saqar.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:41-49/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:41-49/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:41-49/r2.claim: The question about what brought them into Saqar introduces the criminals' narrated answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:41-49/r2.anchor: { ما سلككم فى سقر } بجوابه حكاية لما جرى بين المسؤولين والمجرمين أجابوا بها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r1.claim: Believers first lack knowledge of the damned because each is occupied with himself; God then reveals their enemies burning in Hell to increase the believers' joy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r1.anchor: فكشف الله - لهم عنهم حتى رأوهم في النار وهي تسعر بهم ليقر الله أعينهم بعذابهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r2.claim: The question may express either rebuke or astonishment, and sallakum means inserting someone through a very narrow opening.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r2.anchor: أي أدخلكم أيها المجرمون إدخالا هو في غاية الضيق حتى كأنكم السلك في الثقب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r3.claim: The question lets the saved learn the damned person's own account, increasing their gratitude and serving as a warning to listeners.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r3.anchor: ليزدادوا بذلك غبطة وسرورا بما نجاهم الله من مثل حالهم

DURR-FULL:v8p337/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p337/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p337/r10.claim: In Anas's report, the lowest-ranking person in Hell would ransom himself with the earth's weight in gold, but God recalls easier requests for help and forgiveness that he never made or feared; no one is worse than him.
DURR-FULL:v8p337/r10.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يؤتى بأدنى أهل النار منزلة يوم القيامة فيقول الله له: تفتدى بملء الأرض ذهبا وفضة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273/r3.claim: The criminals say they did not pray or feed the poor, meaning they neither worshipped God nor did good to fellow humans.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273/r3.anchor: أي: ما عبدنا ربنا ولا أحسنا إلى خلقه من جنسنا

QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r13.claim: The question 'what brought you to Saqar?' means 'what put you into it,' as when a thread is inserted into something.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r13.anchor: { ما سلككم } أي أدخلكم { في سقر } كما تقول: سلكت الخيط في كذا أي أدخلته فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r14.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r14.claim: Al-Kalbī says a person in Paradise asks a person in Hell by name; ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and ʿUmar read an explanatory 'so-and-so' gloss, which Ibn al-Anbārī says is not Qurʾān.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r14.anchor: قال الكلبي: فيسأل الرجل من أهل الجنة الرجل من أهل النار باسمه، فيقول له: يا فلان وفي قراءة عبد الله بن الزبير «يا فلان ما سلكك في سقر»؟ وعنه قال: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب «يا فلان ما سلككم في سقر» وهي قراءة على التفسير، لا أنها قرآن كما زعم من طعن في القرآن قاله أبو بكر بن الأنباري.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r15.claim: Alternatively, believers ask angels about their relatives, and the angels in turn ask the polytheists what put them in Saqar.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r15.anchor: وقيل: إن المؤمنين يسألون الملائكة عن أقربائهم، فتسأل الملائكة المشركين فيقولون لهم: { ما سلككم في سقر }.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r16.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r16.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says this supports identifying the people of the right as children, since children do not know sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r16.anchor: قال الفراء: في هذا ما يقوي أن أصحاب اليمين الولدان لأنهم لا يعرفون الذنوب.

TABRISI:74:38-47/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:38-47/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:38-47/r9.claim: The question “What brought you to Saqar?” is a rebuke from the people of Paradise to the people of Hell.
TABRISI:74:38-47/r9.anchor: هذا سؤال توبيخ أي تطلع أهل الجنة على أهل النار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r1.claim: The question can directly explain what the blessed ask, without inserting “saying”; alternatively an implied “saying” clause is circumstantial after “they ask one another.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r1.anchor: بيان للتساؤل من غير حاجة إلى إضمار قول أو هو مقدر بقول وقع حالا من فاعل يتساءلون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r2.claim: One view makes the questioners a group of angels, with the words reporting what the blessed say the angels asked the criminals; the answer is elaborated to make the account more convincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r2.anchor: وقيل المسؤل غير المجرمين كجماعة من الملائكة عليهم السلام وما سلككم الخ حكاية قول المسؤلين عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r3.claim: The question may be genuinely reciprocal, with one group asking another about the criminals; treating the words as quoted speech is needlessly strained, though omission is common in revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن تكون صيغة التفاعل على حقيقتها أي يسأل بعضهم بعضا عن المجرمين وما سلككم حكاية قول المسؤل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r4.claim: The question is likely a rebuke and expression of remorse, since the questioners already know what put the criminals in Hell and the truth will be disclosed that day.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن السؤال سؤال توبيخ وتحسير وإلا فهم عالمون ما الذي أدخلهم النار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r5.speaker: ابن الزبير وعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, and also ʿUmar, are reported to have read “They ask about the criminals, ‘So-and-so, what put you in Saqar?’”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r5.anchor: وروي عبد الله ابن أحمد وجماعة عن ابن الزبير أنه يقرأ يتساءلون عن المجرمين يا فلان ما سلككم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have read “O disbelievers, what put you in Saqar?”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r6.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد وابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ يا أيها الكفار ما سلككم في سقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r1.claim: “In gardens” may attach to “they ask one another,” placed first for emphasis; “asking” is then a circumstantial clause about the people of the right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r1.anchor: حال من { أصحاب اليمين } وهو مناط التفصيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r2.claim: Alternatively, “in gardens” completes an omitted “they are in gardens,” an explanatory resumption; “asking” is circumstantial of the omitted pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r2.anchor: والجملة استئناف بياني لمضمون جملة الاستثناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r3.claim: The reciprocal form can mean the people of the right ask one another about the sinners, with “what put you in Saqar?” explaining their question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r3.anchor: للدلالة على صدور الفعل من جانبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r4.claim: The address in “what put you in Saqar?” implies an omitted questioner: they ask the sinners, rather than the pronoun marking a grammatical shift.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r4.anchor: والتقدير : فيسألون المجرمين ما سلككم في سقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r5.claim: Alternatively, some of those questioned may tell their companions what they said in answer to the questioners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r5.anchor: أو يقول بعض المسؤولين لأصحابهم جوابا لسائليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r6.claim: The plural reciprocal form can instead express repeated questioning or many questioners, rather than an exchange between two sides.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون صيغة التفاعل مستعملة في معنى تكرير الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares the form to collective usage such as “we called one another”: multiple people act from one side, not reciprocally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري في تفسير قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives singular “I called” versus plural “we called,” with analogous collective forms for throwing and seeing the moon.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r9.claim: On the collective reading, the object is omitted and recoverable from the mention of the criminals: they ask about why the criminals entered Saqar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r9.anchor: والتقدير : يتساءلون المجرمين عنهم ، أي عن سبب حصولهم في سقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r10.claim: Salaka originally means to insert something among the parts of another thing, as threading beads; here it metaphorically means thrusting them into Saqar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r10.anchor: وأصل معنى سلكه أدخله بين أجزاء شيء حقيقة ومنه جاء سلك العقد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r1.claim: The commentators gloss salakakum as He admitted you into Saqar.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p411#4/r2.claim: Muqatil explains the question as asking what detained them in Saqar.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r1.claim: S alakakum means “what admitted you into it?”

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r2.claim: The question is not itself a report of the believers asking about sinners; it quotes what those questioned report saying to the sinners and what they answered. The narration is elliptical, as Qurʾānic style often is.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r2.anchor: لأن ما سلككم ليس ببيان للتساؤل عنهم وانما هو حكاية قول المسئولين عنهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r3.claim: Another analysis treats ʿan as an extra particle.

QASHANI:74:38-42/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:38-42/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:38-42/r5.claim: The question they put to the criminals is, “What brought you into Saqar?”
QASHANI:74:38-42/r5.anchor: عن حالهم بقولنا: { ما سلككم في سقر

RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r2.claim: One parse treats “about” as an extra particle: they ask the criminals directly, “What brought you into Saqar?”
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r2.anchor: أن تكون كلمة عن صلة زائدة ، والتقدير : يتساءلون المجرمين

RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the people of the right ask one another about the criminals; al-Kashshaf answers that the criminals recount what happened between them and the questioners.
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r3.anchor: أجاب صاحب ( الكشاف ) عنه فقال : المراد من هذا أن المسؤولين يلقون إلى السائلين

RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r4.claim: A further possibility is that the people of the right asked where the criminals were, then addressed them when they saw them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r4.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر ، وهو أن يكون المراد أن أصحاب اليمين كانوا يتساءلون عن المجرمين أين هم

RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r5.claim: The many implicit elements in the exchange exemplify how often the Qur'an leaves material understood from context.

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r1.claim: The question adds rebuke and humiliation; it asks what detained them in this depth of the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r1.anchor: المقصود من السؤال زيادة التوبيخ والتخجيل ، والمعنى ما حبسكم في هذه الدركة من النار

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r2.claim: The failures to pray and feed the poor mean neglect of obligatory prayer and zakat, since people cannot be punished for omitting non-obligatory acts.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r2.anchor: وهذان يجب أن يكونا محمولين على الصلاة الواجبة ، والزكاة الواجبة لأن ما ليس بواجب

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r3.claim: Their joining those who “delved” means engaging in falsehoods.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r3.anchor: وثالثها : { وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين } والمراد منه الأباطيل

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r4.claim: The “certainty” that finally came to them means death; they denied the resurrection until dying.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r4.anchor: ورابعها : { وكنا نكذب بيوم الدين } أي بيوم القيامة حتى أتانا اليقين ، أي الموت

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r5.claim: The wording apparently says that each member of those groups possessed all four listed traits.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r5.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ يدل على أن كل أحد من أولئك الأقوام كان موصوفا بهذه الخصال الأربعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r6.claim: The author's school cites this verse to argue that unbelievers are punished for neglecting the subsidiary rules of religious law; he says the detailed treatment is in al-Mahsul.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r6.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن الكفار يعذبون بترك فروع الشرائع

RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r7.claim: Although denial of judgment is the worst fault, it comes last to stress that they persisted in it after the preceding three traits.
RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r7.anchor: أريد أنهم بعد اتصافهم بتلك الأمور الثلاثة كانوا مكذبين بيوم الدين ، والغرض تعظيم هذا الذنب

STUDYQURAN:74:40/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r1.claim: The companions of the right ask about fellow believers who failed to act according to revelation and now face this predicament.
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r1.anchor: The companions of the right are said to question one another about the predicament of their fellow believers who had failed to act in accord with the revelation

STUDYQURAN:74:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase simply means they question the sinners directly.
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r2.anchor: Others interpret questioning one another to simply mean“questioning,” indicating that they speak directly to the sinners (Q, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:74:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r3.claim: This is among passages showing that, at least sometimes, people in the Garden and Fire can communicate in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:74:40/r3.anchor: This would then be one of several passages to indicate that in the Hereafter those in the Garden and those in the Fire are, at least on occasion, able to communicate with one another

FARRA:v3p205/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p205/r4.speaker: علي
FARRA:v3p205/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ali identifies them as children; al-Farra finds this more plausible because children had no deeds to bind them, and their question about sinners supports it.
FARRA:v3p205/r4.anchor: وحدثني الفضيل بن عياض عن منصور بن المعتمر عن المنهال رفعه إلى علي قال: «إلا أصحاب اليمين» قال: هم الولدان،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498/r1.claim: The question means, What caused you to enter the Fire?
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498/r1.anchor: {ما سلككم في سقر} ؟ أي ما أدخلكم النار؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r14.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r14.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the question as “What admitted you?”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r14.anchor: {ما سلككم في سقر (42)} (4): قال الكلبي: ما أدخلكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r15.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r15.claim: Muqatil glosses it as “What put you in Saqar?”; he says believers asked the unbelievers left in the Fire after monotheists were taken out what had kept them there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p452/r15.anchor: قال مقاتل: ما جعلكم في سقر. مال: وذلك لما أخرج الله أهل التوحيد من النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:42/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:42/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:42/r1.claim: The question means: what caused you to enter Hell?
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:42/r1.anchor: ما سلككم في سقر } أي: ما أدخلكم جهنم؟

BURHAN:v1p255/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p255/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p255/r7.claim: A single word contains two kāfs without an intervening letter only in the cited forms مناسككم and ما سلككم.
BURHAN:v1p255/r7.anchor: ليس فيه كافان فى كلمة واحدة لا حرف بينهما إلا فى موضعين فى البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r2.claim: Exegetes list entering as one Quranic sense of salaka.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p351/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أنه في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr assimilates سلككم, analogous to مناسككم in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r2.anchor:
وأدغم أبو عمرو " سلككم " وهو نظير
مناسككم

SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r3.claim: ما سلككم may be introduced by an omitted verb of saying; that saying is circumstantial, as they ask those in Hell what brought them there.
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r3.anchor: وقوله " ما سلككم " يجوز أن يكون على إضمار القول، وذلك القول في موضع الحال

SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ما سلككم as the report of what the questioned people asked the criminals, resolving the apparent mismatch.
SAMIN-DURR:74:43/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: كيف طابق قوله " ما سلككم " وهو سؤال المجرمين
